content:
Google is about to restrict the Gemini models available to free users and AI Plus subscribers, in line with the compute usage policy revised in May of this year.

According to a support document updated this week, Gemini App users without a Google AI subscription will only be able to use the (3.5) Flash-Lite model. From October 9, non-paying users will no longer have access to (3.6) Flash or (3.1) Pro.

As for AI Plus subscribers, they will only be able to use Flash-Lite and Flash; the Pro model will no longer be available. These users, who pay US$4.99 per month, will "receive an email explaining when the changes will take effect."

Gemini Model Google AI Plan Flash-Lite Flash Pro Without a plan ✓ X X AI Plus ✓ ✓ X AI Pro ✓ ✓ ✓ AI Ultra ✓ ✓ ✓

AI Pro and AI Ultra users are not affected. In fact, customers paying US$19.99 per month will have access to the Deep Think option, which provides "maximum parallel reasoning" capabilities and is currently limited to the US$99.99 and US$199.99 monthly plans.

Glitter Guru top liked comment:

Argon had better replace Pro, otherwise I expect 4 Pro will be launched alongside Argon. If that doesn't happen and the top model for most users remains the outdated 3.1 Pro, I'll cancel the Pro plan.

Gemini 3.1 Pro on AI Ultra with Deep Think

During October, the Gemini App also appears to be adding "low," "medium," and "high" reasoning intensity options, "applicable to all available models."

Currently, users can only enable the "Extended Thinking: Complex Problem Solving" feature. The three new reasoning intensity levels will align with the existing settings in Google AI Studio and Antigravity.

How Gemini 4 Argon will be positioned remains unclear. Google announced earlier this week that Argon will be offered first to AI Ultra subscribers. The company has not indicated whether Argon will be classified as a Pro model or placed in a brand-new tier above Pro.
